evidence.positive: Against the running app at localhost:55025 (image loop-5ee1adcde, shipped classes) six simultaneous POST /api/app-launch requests were fired for demo tenant patient-1 / patient-2 (start offsets 0-2ms apart, harness scratch/launch.js). All six returned HTTP 200 (e.g. {"i":5,"patient":"patient-1","status":200,"ms":574}). With postgres log_statement='all' enabled, the container log showed each refresh opening its transaction with exactly the two statements the fix adds, in order: "execute <unnamed>: SELECT set_config('lock_timeout', $1, true)" then "execute <unnamed>: SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock($1)" - 6 advisory-lock statements for 6 launches. Per-patient keying was proven directly: an external psql session held pg_advisory_xact_lock(558376238) (= Objects.hash("patient-refresh","demo-demo","patient-1")) inside an open transaction; the concurrent patient-1 launch blocked and then failed after 10230ms with "JDBC exception executing SQL [ERROR: canceling statement due to lock timeout] [SELECT pg_advisory_x...", i.e. it waited on the exact key the fix computes and aborted at the configured 10s bound. The HL7 half of the commit was exercised on the same instance: Four simultaneous SIU^S14 injections (POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send, tenant mayo-mayo) for a PMRN the tenant had never seen all ACKed AA and produced exactly one mayo-mayo patients row, with the log line 'Resolved patient absent from the tenant' - the skeleton insert now resolving through HL7ProcessingContext.findOrCreatePatient under the same lock.
evidence.negative: Two inverse cases were checked on the shipped build. (1) The failure the ticket reports does not occur: across the concurrent runs above, `docker logs ... | grep -c "unexpected row count"` returned 0, and patient-1's patient_conditions table held exactly one row afterwards (id 01a03f65-4ccd-74cc-937c-eeb4f6c453c6, created_date 18:46:39) - replaced once, not duplicated. (2) The silent-duplication ending does not occur either: patient_conditions for patient-2 was deleted to empty, six simultaneous launches were fired, and the table came back with count = 1 (the identical setup produced 4 rows on the pre-fix build). (3) The lock does not over-serialize: while patient-1's key was held externally, a simultaneous patient-2 launch returned HTTP 200 in 280ms rather than blocking - different patients are not serialized against each other.
evidence.red_check: The pre-fix class was compiled and swapped in. `git show 12ae203de^:orci/src/main/java/com/guided/orci/service/PatientService.java` (PatientService.java is unchanged between the fix commit and HEAD, so this is exactly the pre-fix source) was taken, @Slf4j replaced with an explicit org.slf4j.Logger field since lombok is not on the runtime classpath, compiled in-container with javac -cp /app/classes:/app/resources:/app/libs/* and copied over /app/classes/com/guided/orci/service/PatientService.class after backing the shipped class up (md5 aafdddb7d9e14a038914035efcf6a241 -> 7b6ce8bd0c836c1b2f3441367b5b81b6). The container was restarted; a probe launch confirmed zero pg_advisory_xact_lock statements, so the unlocked code was live. Six simultaneous launches for patient-1 then turned red: five of six returned HTTP 500 with org.springframework.orm.ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException / org.hibernate.StaleStateException "Batch update returned unexpected row count from update 0 (expected row count 1 but was 0) [delete from patient_conditions where id=?] for entity [com.guided.orci.models.patient.PatientCondition with id '01a03f60-76ef-7d73-83bd-59c557386fc0']", thrown from com.guided.orci.repository.OperationRepository.findByCaseIdAndPatientId -> OperationService.startOperation -> AppLaunchService.getOrCreatePatientAndOperation - the same three frames as the Sentry stack on the ticket. The silent second ending was reproduced too: with patient-2's patient_conditions emptied first, four simultaneous launches all returned 200 and left 4 duplicate rows. The shipped class was then restored (md5 back to aafdddb7d9e14a038914035efcf6a241, byte-identical to the backup), the container restarted, and the positive case re-run: 6/6 HTTP 200, 6 advisory locks taken, 0 'unexpected row count' errors, patient_conditions back to exactly 1 row. All occurrences of the red string in the container log carry timestamps inside the 18:45:27 red window only.

red_check_signature: unexpected row count from update 0 (expected row count 1 but was 0) [delete from patient_conditions where id=?]
caveats: The demo tenant's EMR fetch never populates family_member_histories, so the collection that actually raced was patient_conditions; the mechanism (orphanRemoval deleting a row a concurrent refresh already deleted) and the failing stack frames are identical to the Sentry report.

Separate pre-existing bug found, not caused by this fix and not fixed by it: four concurrent SIU messages for the same case abort with 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint uk9dj8ufodtosa5mfnq085yr1sh' on the operations insert. Reproduced with an already-existing patient, so it is independent of the patient-refresh lock and worth its own ticket.
Contention was multi-threaded within one JVM against a shared Postgres, not across two application nodes; the advisory lock is cluster-wide by construction but a genuine two-node race was not staged.

patient.refresh-lock.timeout defaults to 10s and is applied with set_config(..., is_local => true), so it bounds every lock wait for the rest of the transaction including the row locks startOperation takes later. Every deployed profile (aws-dev/stage/prod, openshift-guidedor-prod/tst) already sets lock_timeout = '10s' in connection-init-sql, so the statement is a no-op there.
The FDB cloud connector returns 403 in this offline instance, so allergy screening is degraded; it does not touch the refresh path under test.

patient_allergies and patient_medication_allergies grow by one full set on every refresh even single-threaded (4 -> 32 rows over eight sequential launches on patient-1), i.e. those two collections are never orphan-removed at all. That is unrelated to this ticket's race but looks like a real leak.

automation.assessment: The fix already ships strong automated coverage and nothing further is needed for OR-2774 itself. PatientRefreshLockTest covers the no-op, missing-tenant and bound-before-waiting branches; PatientRefreshLockPostgresConcurrencyIntegrationTest covers same-patient blocking, different-patient non-blocking, same-pmrn-different-tenant non-blocking and timeout abort against a real Postgres; PatientRefreshConcurrencyIntegrationTest covers both end-to-end failure modes (StaleStateException when rows exist, silent duplication when they do not); MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest now asserts the processor routes the skeleton insert through the context and never calls patientRepository.save directly. The only gaps worth locking in belong to the separate operations-insert race found during this run.
proposed_tests: Regression test for the separate defect: concurrent SIU^S14 messages for one (patient, case) must not abort on the operations unique constraint uk9dj8ufodtosa5mfnq085yr1sh - file under a new ticket, not OR-2774.
Optional supplemental check that repeated patient refreshes leave patient_allergies and patient_medication_allergies at a stable row count, covering the non-orphan-removed collections noted above.

jira_comment:
Validated against a disposable local instance built from 5ee1adcde (main), demo and mayo tenants, using the real /api/app-launch and HL7 admin-send paths.

Positive: six simultaneous app launches for one demo patient all returned 200. Postgres statement logging shows each refresh opening its transaction with SELECT set_config('lock_timeout', ..., true) followed by SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(...), one per refresh. Holding that patient's advisory key from an outside psql session made the launch block and abort after 10.2 seconds on exactly that statement, which confirms the key is derived from tenant plus pmrn as intended.

Negative: no ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException in any run, the patient's condition rows stayed at exactly one (replaced, not duplicated), and a simultaneous launch for a different patient completed in 280ms rather than queueing, so the lock is per patient and not global.

Red check: the pre-fix PatientService was compiled from the parent commit and swapped into the running container. Five of six simultaneous launches then failed with StaleStateException "Batch update returned unexpected row count from update 0 ... [delete from patient_conditions where id=?]" from OperationRepository.findByCaseIdAndPatientId via OperationService.startOperation via AppLaunchService.getOrCreatePatientAndOperation, the same frames as the Sentry stack on this ticket. The silent second ending reproduced as well: starting from an empty collection, four concurrent launches all returned 200 and left four duplicate rows. The shipped class was restored, checksum verified byte-identical, and the positive case re-run clean.

The HL7 half was exercised too: four concurrent SIU^S14 messages for an unknown PMRN produced exactly one patient row.

Automation: the existing unit, Testcontainers and end-to-end concurrency tests added with the fix already cover this thoroughly and nothing further is proposed for this ticket.

One unrelated finding for a separate ticket: concurrent SIU messages for the same case still abort on the operations unique constraint uk9dj8ufodtosa5mfnq085yr1sh. It reproduces with an already-existing patient, so it is independent of this fix and pre-dates it.
